raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

**This draft PR is for demonstration purposes only.** It demonstrates MXFP8 linear operations on gfx950 using AITER activation quantization and `hipb_mm` with swizzled operand scales.

Requires [ROCm/aiter#6582](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6582) and hipBLASLt >= 1.3.

## Claims

- Enable the demonstration by setting `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR_HIPBMM=1` before starting vLLM. It is disabled by default.
- Swizzle weight scales once during loading and produce swizzled activation scales during quantization; FP8 weight values keep their ordinary layout.
- Support `torch.compile` through registered custom operations and their fake implementations.

## Validation

### Model prefill

We requantized the original BF16 Muse Glimmer 30B and Qwen3.8-27B checkpoints to MXFP8 for this demonstration. Qwen3-32B uses the existing INCModel MXFP8 checkpoint.

Measured on one MI355X (gfx950) using the official [ROCm 10.1 vLLM image](https://hub.docker.com/r/rocm/vllm/tags?name=rocm10.1.0_ubuntu24.04_py3.14-pytorch_2.13.0_vllm-0.29.0), which contains vLLM `0.29.1.dev0+g98dff2a81.d20261002.rocm101` and PyTorch 2.13.0. Both implementations used the same image and MXFP8 checkpoints; native vLLM used unswizzled scales, and AITER + hipBLASLt used swizzled scales.

Each latency is the arithmetic mean of model prefill execution times from two independent performance processes, measured from profiler timestamps. Each process ran one unprofiled warm-up with the same shape for each prompt before measurement. The maximum spread between repeats was 3.274%, measured as `(max/min - 1) × 100`. Speedup is native latency divided by AITER latency.

| Model checkpoint | Prefill tokens | Native vLLM (ms) | AITER + hipBLASLt (ms) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [INCModel/Qwen3-32B-MXFP8-CT-AutoRound](https://huggingface.co/INCModel/Qwen3-32B-MXFP8-CT-AutoRound) | 16384 | 2207.97 | 1444.47 | 1.53× |
| [INCModel/Qwen3-32B-MXFP8-CT-AutoRound](https://huggingface.co/INCModel/Qwen3-32B-MXFP8-CT-AutoRound) | 2048 | 196.55 | 105.40 | 1.86× |
| [rkayaith/Muse-Glimmer-30B-mxfp8](https://huggingface.co/rkayaith/Muse-Glimmer-30B-mxfp8) | 16384 | 1478.95 | 852.26 | 1.74× |
| [rkayaith/Muse-Glimmer-30B-mxfp8](https://huggingface.co/rkayaith/Muse-Glimmer-30B-mxfp8) | 2048 | 158.81 | 89.84 | 1.77× |
| [talumbau/Qwen3.8-27B-mxfp8](https://huggingface.co/talumbau/Qwen3.8-27B-mxfp8) | 16384 | 1552.26 | 931.46 | 1.67× |
| [talumbau/Qwen3.8-27B-mxfp8](https://huggingface.co/talumbau/Qwen3.8-27B-mxfp8) | 2048 | 162.51 | 157.43 | 1.03× |

These runs produced matching smoke-token outputs between the native and AITER paths. They do not establish full model accuracy.

### Kernel validation

The same kernel implementation passed **65 test cases** on MI355X (gfx950) with vLLM 0.31.0, ROCm 7.2.3, and hipBLASLt 1.5:

```sh
HIP_ONLINE_TUNING=0 PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1 PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 pytest -q -x --noconftest \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py::test_rocm_mxfp8_linear_matches_dequant_reference \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py::test_gfx950_scale_layout_linear_compiles
```

The tests compare native and AITER outputs against dequantized references and check compiled execution with padded scales.

## Details

```sh
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR_HIPBMM=1
```

The selection log reports `Using RocmHipbmmMxfp8LinearKernel for MXFP8 GEMM`. The implementation requires `K` divisible by 128 and uses `BLK32_UE8M0_32_8_EXT` for both operands with automatic hipBLASLt algorithm selection. It also respects an explicitly set `HIP_ONLINE_TUNING`; validation used `0`.

Separate standalone validation found correctness failures for two prefill shapes with `K=29568` in the existing AITER quantizer. The model checks above do not cover those shapes.

This is a hipBLASLt backend for gfx950 dense MXFP8 linears. Related [#60169](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60169) uses FlyDSL for DeepSeek's 32x32 block scales, and [#60384](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60384) targets gfx942 decode with an A16W8 assembly kernel. Neither adds this `hipb_mm` path.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.

+def shuffle_mxfp8_scale_gfx950(scale: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Convert row-major MXFP8 scales to gfx950 ``32x8`` storage."""
+    if scale.ndim != 2:
+        raise ValueError(f"scale must be two-dimensional, got shape {scale.shape}")
+
+    rows, columns = scale.shape
+    padded_rows = (rows + 31) // 32 * 32
+    padded_columns = (columns + 7) // 8 * 8
+    padded = torch.zeros(
+        (padded_rows, padded_columns), dtype=scale.dtype, device=scale.device
+    )
+    padded[:rows, :columns] = scale
+    return (
+        padded.view(padded_rows // 32, 2, 16, padded_columns // 8, 2, 4)
+        .permute(0, 3, 5, 2, 4, 1)
+        .contiguous()
+        .view(padded_rows, padded_columns)
+    )
+
+
+def _rocm_mxfp8_dot_scaled_mm_gfx950_impl(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    x_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    w: torch.Tensor,
+    w_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    output_dtype: torch.dtype,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    M, K = x.shape
+    N = w.shape[0]
+    assert K % 128 == 0, f"input columns must be divisible by 128, got {K}"
+    expected_scale_columns = (K // MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE + 7) // 8 * 8
+    assert x_scale.shape == ((M + 31) // 32 * 32, expected_scale_columns)
+    assert w_scale.shape == ((N + 31) // 32 * 32, expected_scale_columns)
+    assert x_scale.dtype == MXFP8_SCALE_DTYPE
+    assert w_scale.dtype == MXFP8_SCALE_DTYPE
+    assert x_scale.is_contiguous()
+    assert w_scale.is_contiguous()
+    from aiter import HipblasLtMatmulScaleMode, hipb_mm
+
+    from vllm._aiter_ops import _ensure_hipb_mm_extension_initialized
+
+    _ensure_hipb_mm_extension_initialized()
+    mode = HipblasLtMatmulScaleMode.BLK32_UE8M0_32_8_EXT
+    return hipb_mm(
+        x,
+        w.mT,
+        solution_index=-1,
+        out_dtype=output_dtype,
+        scaleA=x_scale,
+        scaleB=w_scale,
+        scaleA_mode=mode,
+        scaleB_mode=mode,
+    )
+
+
+def _rocm_mxfp8_dot_scaled_mm_fake(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    x_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    w: torch.Tensor,
+    w_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    output_dtype: torch.dtype,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    del x_scale, w_scale
+    return torch.empty(
+        (x.shape[0], w.shape[0]),
+        dtype=output_dtype,
+        device=x.device,
+    )
+
+
+def _rocm_aiter_mxfp8_quantize_gfx950_impl(
+    input: torch.Tensor,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    from aiter import dynamic_per_group_scaled_quant
+
+    output, scale = _allocate_mxfp8_quantize_gfx950_outputs(input)
+    dynamic_per_group_scaled_quant(
+        output,
+        input,
+        scale,
+        group_size=MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE,
+        shuffle_scale=True,
+    )
+    return output, scale
+
+
+def _rocm_aiter_mxfp8_quantize_gfx950_fake(
+    input: torch.Tensor,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    return _allocate_mxfp8_quantize_gfx950_outputs(input)
+
+
+def _allocate_mxfp8_quantize_gfx950_outputs(
+    input: torch.Tensor,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    rows, columns = input.shape
+    assert input.dtype in {
+        torch.float16,
+        torch.bfloat16,
+    }, f"input dtype must be float16 or bfloat16, got {input.dtype}"
+    assert columns % 128 == 0, f"input columns must be divisible by 128, got {columns}"
+    padded_rows = (rows + 31) // 32 * 32
+    scale_columns = (columns // MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE + 7) // 8 * 8
+    return (
+        torch.empty_like(input, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn),
+        torch.empty(
+            (padded_rows, scale_columns),
+            dtype=MXFP8_SCALE_DTYPE,
+            device=input.device,
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+def _mxfp8_dot_scaled_linear_gfx950(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    w: torch.Tensor,
+    w_scale: torch.Tensor,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    x_q, x_scale = torch.ops.vllm.rocm_aiter_mxfp8_quantize_gfx950(x)
+    return torch.ops.vllm.rocm_mxfp8_dot_scaled_mm_gfx950(
+        x_q,
+        x_scale,
+        w,
+        w_scale,
+        x.dtype,
+    )
+
+
+class RocmHipbmmMxfp8LinearKernel(RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel):
+    """gfx950 MXFP8 linear using AITER quantization and standalone hipb_mm."""
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+        weight = layer.weight.data
+        N, K = weight.shape
+        assert K % 128 == 0, f"weight columns must be divisible by 128, got {K}"
+        scale_k = K // MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE
+        weight_scale = layer.weight_scale.data[:N, :scale_k].contiguous()
+        layer.weight = Parameter(weight.contiguous(), requires_grad=False)
+        layer.weight_scale = Parameter(
+            shuffle_mxfp8_scale_gfx950(weight_scale), requires_grad=False
+        )
+
+    def apply_weights(
+        self,
+        layer: torch.nn.Module,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        bias: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if layer.weight_scale.dtype != MXFP8_SCALE_DTYPE:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Expected {MXFP8_SCALE_DTYPE} weight_scale, got "
+                f"{layer.weight_scale.dtype}."
+            )
+        assert x.shape[-1] % 128 == 0, (
+            f"input columns must be divisible by 128, got {x.shape[-1]}"
+        )
+        out_shape = (*x.shape[:-1], layer.weight.shape[0])
+        x2d = x.reshape(-1, x.shape[-1])
+        out = _mxfp8_dot_scaled_linear_gfx950(
+            x2d, layer.weight, layer.weight_scale
+        ).reshape(out_shape)
+        if bias is not None:
+            out = out + bias
+        return out
+
+
+direct_register_custom_op(
+    op_name="rocm_aiter_mxfp8_quantize_gfx950",
+    op_func=_rocm_aiter_mxfp8_quantize_gfx950_impl,
+    fake_impl=_rocm_aiter_mxfp8_quantize_gfx950_fake,
+)
+
+direct_register_custom_op(
+    op_name="rocm_mxfp8_dot_scaled_mm_gfx950",
+    op_func=_rocm_mxfp8_dot_scaled_mm_gfx950_impl,
+    fake_impl=_rocm_mxfp8_dot_scaled_mm_fake,
+)

 ):

PRs do not trigger a full CI run by default. Reviewers with write access and configured trusted contributors can comment `/ci run` for upstream CI or `/amd-ci run` for AMD CI only whenever CI signals are needed.

Once the PR is approved or has the `ready` label, the PR author can also use the corresponding `/ci run`, `/ci retry`, and `/ci cancel` commands, or their `/amd-ci` variants. New commits do not start upstream CI automatically.

If you have any questions, please reach out to us on Slack at https://slack.vllm.ai.
